incident_bot: PAGER — Dedicated pool 'verdant-prod-pool' GPU saturation detected for tenant 'verdant-enterprise'. Priority: P1

sam.oncall: paging in. I'm on-call for this shift. Anyone in runtime or infra? @devin.runtime @kevin.sre

maria.sre: I'll join. seeing huge queue on pool. GPU util 99% on all nodes, pending requests ~320, avg latency 4.8s -> errors

devin.runtime: looking at scheduler. Autoscaler didn't trigger; scale events suppressed due to tenant pinning. This is single-tenant reserved pool hitting concurrency limits.

kevin.sre: confirmed. metrics:
- pool: verdant-prod-pool
- nodes: 8/8 gpus
- gpu_util: 98-100%
- pending_reqs: 318
- model: gpt-medium-8k-quant

jenna.eng: any chance to enable emergency burst? runbook says request burst-override to allocator team.

maria.sre: I'm starting bridge with allocator. tagging CS for customer comms. @sylvia.cs

sylvia.cs: I'll open a customer bridge and notify Verdant account team. ETA on mitigation?

devin.runtime: options:
1) burst-override (spin up 2 reserved burst nodes) -> add ~4 GPUs, ~7-10min
2) move Verdant to fallback model (smaller model) if acceptable -> instant but regresses quality
3) throttle non-critical endpoints (batching) -> immediate partial relief

sam.oncall: prioritize 1+3. start burst-override, apply temporary throttles for long-running jobs and embeddings. We need to keep SLA for core endpoints.

maria.sre: applying throttles: applying rate limit to /v1/embedding and lowering max_tokens to 1024 for chat-stream for this tenant.

devin.runtime: issuing burst-override request now:

```
POST /internal/allocator/burst-requests
{ "pool":"verdant-prod-pool","gpus":4,"reason":"P1 tenant saturation","owner":"sam.oncall" }
```

allocator_bot: Burst request received (id: br-9923). Allocating nodes from spare capacity. Estimated attach: 6m.

kevin.sre: meanwhile isolating tenant traffic to dedicated queue to avoid head-of-line blocking for other tenants on shared infra. Running iptables qdisc on edge for Verdant.

juan.monitoring: alert: queue length falling -> 318 -> 210 -> 125 (5m)

devin.runtime: burst nodes attached. New nodes visible: 4 GPUs online. GPUs assigned to pool replicas for verdant.

maria.sre: util dropped to 75% across pool. pending_reqs 42. Starting to relax throttles slowly. flagging for customer update.

sylvia.cs: on customer bridge: Verdant ops appreciates the quick action. They asked about root cause and long-term fix.

sam.oncall: root cause: pool configured as reserved with pinning + autoscaler suppressed for tenant to avoid noisy neighbors; load spike exceeded planned concurrency for Verdant's reserved capacity. Immediate mitigations: burst override + temporary throttling + request routing isolation. Follow-ups: update capacity planning, allow emergency autoscale exceptions, and add early-warning alerts on queue depth.

jenna.eng: I'll open a post-incident ticket with suggested changes: (a) add 'burstable' flag to reserved pools, (b) grade-based auto-exceptions, (c) adapt runbook to auto-request burst when pending_reqs>200 for >2m.

maria.sre: handing off to kevin for follow-up work. I'm switching to oncall standby. @kevin.sre please coordinate with allocator and infra teams.

kevin.sre: ack. I'll take it. creating follow-up RFC and incident writeup. closing on-call thread here. :white_check_mark:

incident_bot: INCIDENT CLOSED — Verdant dedicated pool saturation mitigated, state: degraded->stable. Duration: 42m. Postmortem requested.
